title: alacritty is not properly working in tabbed
body:
`tabbed -c alacritty --embed`
Alacritty "not responds" to keypresses when tabbed (exactly like keys aren't pressed), but mouse is working (selection/copy/hints).

Versions: alacritty 0.12.3, tabbed 0.7 (0.6 has same behaviour), Linux

`tabbed` itself is functional (tested with xterm). I've tried to compare alacritty logs (tabbed and non-tabbed) but failed to find anything relevant:
[Alacritty.log](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/files/13199094/Alacritty.log)
[Alacritty-embed.log](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/files/13199095/Alacritty-embed.log)
(in both cases I just typed `123` and Alt-F4 to close)

upd: there is a small difference if alacritty embedded "separately" (run `tabbed`, then `alacritty --embed $XID`): when key is pressed, cursor changes from beam shape (as defined in config) to "cell" (rectangular) shape. This is **not** happening if using `tabbed -c alacritty --embed`

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
upd1: This is **not** a "redraw" problem. Seems the shell process don't receive input from `alacritty`. 
`alacritty --embed 0x8c00003 -e /bin/bash -c read` cannot be closed by pressing `Return`.

comments.body: Would be better to test outside of VirtualBox. Generally, you can swap out your WM by changing the way your login manager or desktop environment gets invoked (for example, I load `i3` from my login shell's init-rc file). Since cinnamon seems like it's doing everything, you may have to rewire it at a lower level than you are comfortable with. As I understand things, it should be possible to tell Mint Linux to load another DE/WM, however I can't really help you with that myself.

comments.body:
And other terminals work just fine, correct? Also are you starting new Alacritty windows, or processes?

I'd assume the logs you've posted in the initial issue comment are identical to what you're experiencing now? These suggest that Alacritty is receiving the key events, but it is not the target of those events (instead they're sent to a different application).

yes

How can I debug the target of received messages? 

… I should mention that last time __existing__ tabbed alacritty process had stopped responding to keypresses – the same way as all tabbed alacritty processes invoked after that.

Another thought – how only keyboard events may be wrongly destined while mouse aren't?

I've updated nvidia-drivers few hours ago (because there were some glitches – rare and minor but recurring). At the moment alacritty works fine and I'm keeping an eye on it.

> Could you make sure to try spawning Alacritty separately with the --embed option?

Yes, tabbed surely spawns new process for every tab. But to my big surprise, when I checked a processes, I've found 2 orphaned `alacritty --embed 109051907` processes (no errors in their logs, no tabbed processes as they were all closed at that moment, no any issues). Since I never invoked alacritty separately this time, it may be a bug – though it needs further investigation.

> Alacritty instances outside of tabbed still work just fine

Non-tabbed instances __always__ work fine, only tabbed instances are affected by issue

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Interesting thing I've just noticed, I put all together:
1. `tabbed -c alacritty --embed` – has an issue
2. `tabbed; alacritty --embed $xid` – has an issue
3. `tabbed -c xterm -into` – works fine
4. `tabbed; xterm -into $xid` – **also has an issue!**

... more, soon after I caught issue with `xterm`, it stops working even when **not** tabbed. The most funny part is that `xterm` worked fine at first, then stop working after 1st keypress (I could type only one char) and, at last, stopped working at all.

and more, I've caught interesting warning when running cinnamon in terminal:
```
Window manager warning: Window 0x3000003 has property _NET_WM_NAME
that was expected to have type UTF8_STRING format 8
and actually has type COMPOUND_TEXT format 8 n_items 0.
This is most likely an application bug, not a window manager bug.
The window has title="tabbed-0.7 :: xterm -into 50331651" class="tabbed" name="tabbed"
```

About `orphaned` alacritty instances: it was `tabbed` bug, though I could easily fix it.
Summing all things up, seems that `tabbed` is the first candidate to investigate. 

Saying it again, just to clarify things – the was no issues like this (at all) before `tabbed`.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Considering that Alacritty doesn't really do anything special for `tabbed` to work, I think it's most likely a WM issue.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: As for me – it is obviously not an `alacritty` issue but there is no any evidences that `cinnamon` doing something wrong. On the other side, `tabbed` code is buggy and obsolete in some places (I already fixed 2 bugs as for now) and should not been advised for `tabbing` anything – until it's code is revised.
